maria (platform): Quick follow-up on edge lifecycle + streaming backpressure. Proposal: per-connection token-window + per-route admission queue to avoid head-of-line blocking when slow clients stream. Prototype sketch below — comments?

ajay (edge): I like the admission queue but worried about queue growth for large numbers of idle streams. Two quick notes: 1) use a soft token-window (tokens/sec) not absolute tokens to prevent burst backlog; 2) admission should be prioritized by route SLO & client tier.

sam (runtime): +1. Also need to consider retries/hedging interactions — if we enqueue retry attempts they can amplify load. Suggest adding "retry-origin" metadata and a small retry admission budget per node. Example config snippet: 
```
route: /v1/chat
admission:
  max_inflight_per_conn: 4
  token_rate: 20/s
  retry_budget: 0.1
```

ajay (edge): Good call. For streaming checkpoints, we can propagate a short resume-token in the trailers so client reconnects pick up without replaying full prompt. That reduces duplication for retries. Security: opaque HMAC using connection id.

maria (platform): Nice — can we keep compatibility with existing frontdoor? Need a migration path: 1) opt-in flag per route; 2) gradual canary per region; 3) metrics: per-route queue-depth, resume-success, duplicate-tokens.

ci-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: canary/edge-backpressure/v1 -> deployment started :rocket:

sam (runtime): One more thought — quantized models: smaller kernels reduce per-token CPU but increase KV cache churn; admission should be model-aware. Maybe admission score = tokens * model_weight.

ajay (edge): Agreed. I'll draft an RFC with acceptance criteria and perf targets (p99 latency < 250ms for small requests, duplicate-token < 0.5%). Will ping you both when ready.

maria (platform): Thanks, sgtm. I can add rollout steps & SLO adjustments. :thumbsup:
